records.source: MPR-SAT-FE-69-9 (AS-506 flight evaluation), Table 20-1 Total Vehicle Mass - S-IC Burn Phase, actual: LOX below tank 21,868 kg and RP-1 below tank 5,983 kg at hold-down arm release, 18,761 kg and 5,958 kg at outboard engine cutoff; stations from the MSFC/Boeing drawing 'Saturn V Apollo Flight Configuration' (bottom of LOX tank 772.00 in, bottom of fuel tank 225.00 in, gimbal plane 100.00 in). NTRS 19900066485.
records.variant: AS-506 S-IC LOX and RP-1 suction lines (propellant below the tanks)
records.conditions: The line propellant is carved from the stage load (LOX 1,500,418 to 1,478,550 kg in the tank, RP-1 646,854 to 640,871 kg) and modelled as header stores that feed only after the tanks are empty, as the lines are the last to drain. Point stations: LOX lines midway between the LOX tank bottom (19.6 m) and the F-1 pump inlets (estimated 3.5 m), X-station 11.6 m (part-local -9.42 m); RP-1 lines midway between the fuel tank bottom (5.7 m) and the pumps, X-station 4.6 m (-16.42 m).
records.uncertainty: Line centroids +/-2 m (route through the fuel-tank tunnels not dimensioned on the drawing); masses as reconstructed.

records.source: MPR-SAT-FE-69-9, Saturn V Launch Vehicle Flight Evaluation Report AS-506 Apollo 11 Mission (MSFC, 1969-09-20), Table 20-10 Mass Characteristics Comparison, S-IC stage dry, actual; NTRS 19900066485, https://archive.org/download/nasa_techdoc_19900066485/19900066485.pdf
records.variant: AS-506 S-IC dry structure (tank part beside the 42,000 kg F-1 cluster part)
records.conditions: Solves the S-IC dry composite (F-1 cluster part, uniform cylinder centred at X-station -0.03 m, plus this part) for the reconstructed dry CG X-station 9.368 m; the X-station origin lies 2.930 m above the F-1 exit planes (MSFC drawing). Value is from the part centre (X-station 21.02 m).
records.uncertainty: The model's S-IC dry mass is 135,322 kg against the reconstructed 130,422 kg (a 4,347 kg derived allocation and residual items modelled as dry); their stations are unknown, so the composite CG carries about +/-0.3 m.

records.source: MPR-SAT-FE-69-9 (AS-506 flight evaluation) Table 20-10, S-IC stage dry actual pitch inertia 16.578e6 kg m2 and roll inertia 2.591e6 kg m2; NTRS 19900066485
records.variant: AS-506 S-IC dry structure, central radii of gyration of the tank part
records.conditions: Transverse 10.764 m and axial 4.693 m solve the composite (uniform-cylinder F-1 cluster part plus this part at its derived centre) for the reconstructed S-IC dry pitch and roll inertia about the dry CG.
records.uncertainty: Inherits the dry-mass allocation difference (about 4 %); the cluster part's own uniform-cylinder inertia is an approximation.

records.source: MSFC/Boeing drawing 'Saturn V Apollo Flight Configuration' (Saturn Apollo 500 series, sheets 1-2), S-IC stations: bottom of fuel tank 225.00 in, top of fuel tank 742.00 in, bottom of LOX tank 772.00 in, S-IC/S-II interstage bottom 1541.00 in, LOX tank length 769.00 in, fuel tank length 517.00 in, diameter 396 in; http://heroicrelics.org/info/saturn-v/sat-v-apollo-flight-config/Saturn%20V%20Apollo%20Flight%20Configuration%20(medium).pdf. Densities: LOX saturated liquid at the normal boiling point 1141 kg/m3 (NIST Chemistry WebBook, oxygen); RP-1 807 kg/m3, centre of the MIL-DTL-25576 specification range 799-815 kg/m3 at 15.6 C.
records.variant: AS-506 S-IC RP-1 (aft) and LOX (forward) tanks
records.conditions: Each resource settles as a liquid column on its tank's equivalent flat bottom (NASA SP-106, Abramson 1966, section 2.3: a domed bottom replaced by the flat bottom holding equal liquid volume). Each bulkhead dome is 137 in (3.480 m) deep: Y-ring to apex on the drawing (605.00 to 742.00 in; 772.00 to 909.00 in; 1404.00 to 1541.00 in). An ellipsoidal dome of depth d holds the volume of a cylinder 2d/3 long, so the equivalent ends lie d/3 inside the apexes. Inner radius 198 in (5.029 m). Part-local stations (part centre at X-station 21.02 m): RP-1 -14.145 to -3.334 m, LOX -0.252 to 16.961 m. The resulting capacities (685 t RP-1, 1,543 t LOX) leave 5.6 % and 2.8 % ullage over the AS-506 loads.
records.uncertainty: Exact while the free surface is in the barrel; once it falls into the lower dome the column centroid is low by up to d/6 (0.58 m) for the remaining liquid. Below-tank propellant (feed lines, about 28 t at release) is modelled inside the tanks. Loading temperatures change densities by about 1 %.

records.source: MSFC/Boeing drawing 'Saturn V Apollo Flight Configuration': S-II LOX tank equator X-station 1848 in (46.939 m), S-II top forward skirt 2519.00 in (63.982 m), stage diameter 396 in. Densities: LOX 1141 kg/m3, LH2 70.85 kg/m3 (saturated liquids at the normal boiling point, NIST Chemistry WebBook).
records.variant: AS-506 S-II LOX (aft, ellipsoidal) and LH2 (forward) tanks
records.conditions: The LOX tank is an ellipsoid centred on the drawing's equator, semi-axis b estimated as 0.69 of the 5.029 m inner radius (the S-IC dome ratio, 137/198 in). Its equivalent cylinder (NASA SP-106 equal-volume flat bottom) spans the equator +/- 2b/3; LH2 stands on the LOX tank's equivalent top (the common bulkhead) and reaches the forward skirt. Part-local (part centre at X-station 56.02 m): LOX -11.394 to -6.768 m, LH2 -6.768 to 7.96 m.
records.uncertainty: The S-II dome ratio and LH2 top are estimates; stations +/-1 m. The drawing gives only the LOX equator and skirt stations.
